task: If you reach the exit, you must have flipped the switch first.

calls.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: the Precedence clause has its propositions in the wrong order. The task 'If you reach the exit, you must have flipped the switch first' needs Precedence(switch_toggled, at_exit) hard: at_exit may not happen before switch_toggled has happened. The candidate's Precedence(at_exit, switch_toggled) says the opposite — switch_toggled may not happen before the first at_exit, as the compiled machine confirms: toggling the switch before reaching the exit pays -10 and falls into the rejecting state u1, while reaching the exit without a prior flip is not a violation. Reverse the propositions to (switch_toggled, at_exit) and keep the clause hard; add nothing else, since at_exit is only the condition of an 'if' and gets no Existence (the rule-only warning is valid).

NO CHANGES NEEDED: the task is an 'if' restriction — 'If you reach the exit, you must have flipped the switch first' — so the single hard Precedence(switch_toggled, at_exit) captures it exactly: at_exit may not occur before the first switch_toggled, and it holds vacuously when the exit is never reached. Reaching the exit is only the condition of the 'if', not a commanded goal, so no Existence(at_exit) is due; the empty FINAL_STATES with the rule-only warning is the expected shape for this wording.
